theme: Code-health defects and their look-alikes in a Node.js + TypeScript parcel shipping rates & label service

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: computeSurcharges decides every surcharge in one method: nested branches per carrier, service level, zone, parcel shape and declared value, with compound conditions. Well over any reasonable decision-point budget, and each branch is a distinct path that needs its own test.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The same method nests its branches four levels deep (carrier, service level, zone, parcel shape) with flag variables and early continues: a reader has to hold the whole decision tree to change one surcharge.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: LabelService parses label requests, validates addresses, prices the shipment, picks a carrier, renders the label, writes files and an index, sends the customer e-mail, keeps statistics and purges old labels: more than thirty methods and several hundred lines spanning at least five unrelated responsibilities. The whole class is the site.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The file holding LabelService runs to well over 500 significant lines of hand-written code, far beyond what one module of this service should hold; the size is the symptom of the god class, and a reviewer would ask for it to be split along its responsibilities.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: render writes the whole ZPL label in one function of well over a hundred lines: sender, recipient, routing, barcode, service box, references and the receipt stub, each a section a reader has to scroll through.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The rate-request building and the parcel mapping were copied from the Corvid adapter and are already drifting (one rounds weights up, the other does not): a fix to one copy will be missed in the other.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: CarrierAccountManager holds four groups of fields and methods that never touch each other: API credentials, a request rate limit, an audit trail and the webhook signing secret. Four classes in one.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A TODO comment recording known unfinished work in the production adapter (multi-piece shipments are sent as single parcels).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A HACK comment marking a workaround in the shared label path (the Corvid label is re-rotated after rendering).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: @ts-ignore with no reason hides a real type error: the optional contact e-mail is assigned to a field typed as always present, so the e-mail step later reads undefined.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A bare file-wide eslint-disable with no rule list and no reason switches every lint rule off for the adapter, which is how its unchecked any casts got past review.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A config block turns the type-safety and promise rules (no-floating-promises, no-explicit-any, no-non-null-assertion, no-empty, ban-ts-comment, ...) off for the label pipeline with no reason given: the project-level suppression that lets the plants in that module through the lint gate.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The old label-number scheme left behind as commented-out code instead of being deleted (version control keeps it).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: An empty catch around the customer e-mail: any failure to send vanishes without a log line or a metric, and the customer silently gets no label.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A private method that nothing calls: dead code kept in the god class.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: An exported function that no module, tool or test imports: dead code at module level.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A lower-case case label under switch (code.toUpperCase()): it can never match, so that arm is unreachable (the intended 'ALDER' alias was never served).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: RateCalculator.quote is marked @deprecated in favour of quoteAll, yet the label service still calls it.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: voidLabel throws a 'Not implemented' error although the API exposes label voiding for every carrier: a placeholder reachable in production.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: isRemoteArea ignores its input and returns false, so the remote-area surcharge the calculator depends on never applies: a stub left in production.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: An unparsable transit-days value from the carrier silently becomes 3 days, with no log line and no signal to the caller: delivery promises are made up.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A catch whose only statement rethrows the caught error unchanged: it adds nothing and suggests handling that does not exist.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The carrier's JSON response body is cast to any and its fields read directly: a changed or failed response turns into undefined amounts deep in pricing instead of a validation error at the boundary.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: tools/tsconfig.json compiles the rate-card CLI with strictNullChecks switched off while the service has it on, so null and undefined flow unchecked through the tools. Repository-level: strict-null posture is a property of the build configuration, reported without a line.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: LabelService silences null checking with non-null assertions (!) on values that really can be missing: a carrier lookup by code, an optional sender address, a map lookup by label id and a find over rate quotes. Repository-level: assertion density is reported without a line.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: printerName is optional and treated as possibly undefined one line earlier (printerName?.trim()), then dereferenced unguarded; it is undefined whenever the option is omitted. The tools compile without strict null checks (CH-024), so the compiler does not catch it.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The label route starts archiving the created label and neither awaits nor handles the promise: an archive failure is an unhandled rejection (which terminates Node by default) and the response claims an archived label that may not exist.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: files.forEach(async ...) drops each import's promise: the command reports success and exits before the imports have finished, and a failed import is an unhandled rejection.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The async request-path method load reads the label file with readFileSync, blocking the event loop (and every other request) for the duration of the disk read.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: download fetches the rate card with no AbortSignal and no timeout: a hung rate-card host holds the refresh (and shutdown) forever; the carrier adapters show the codebase's own convention of passing a signal.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A pino log call whose message is a template literal interpolating runtime values: the values are baked into the message text instead of logged as fields, so the line cannot be queried or aggregated.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A debug log call serialises every quote (JSON.stringify over a mapped array) on every request even when debug logging is off.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The configured cache lifetime is stored and never read; isStale re-spells the default instead, so configuring the TTL changes nothing.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The cache creates and owns a RefreshTimer (a disposable class) but its dispose() never disposes it: the interval keeps running after the cache is disposed.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A regular expression pulls the error code out of the JSON error body, in a module that already parses JSON: it breaks on whitespace, key order or escaping that JSON.parse handles.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: lp is spawned with stdout and stderr both piped; only stdout is read while the code waits for exit, so a printer that writes enough to stderr fills the pipe and the print hangs.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: fitToWidth drops the last character while the measured width (which includes fixed margins) exceeds the field: when the margins alone exceed it, the loop runs past the empty string and never ends.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: importFolder changes the working directory and restores it only on the straight-line path: an import error leaves the process in the drop folder.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Inside the per-parcel loop the oversize surcharge is decided by parcels[0] instead of parcels[i]: every parcel is charged (or not) according to the first one.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The #ttlMs field is written in the constructor and read nowhere: dead state (the mechanism behind CH-033).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: #refreshTimer is assigned in the constructor and read nowhere, not even by dispose(): dead state, the field-level face of CH-034 (one fix, disposing it, clears both).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: importFolder and importArchive repeat the same change-directory, list, parse and change-back sequence with local edits; one withWorkingDirectory helper (with its restore in a finally) would replace both and fix CH-038 on the way.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: carrier-registry imports the Corvid adapter, and the adapter imports a runtime constant back from carrier-registry: a value-level import cycle whose evaluation order decides whether the constant is initialised. The site is the registry's import block.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A domain value object imports from the infrastructure layer (the carrier prefix table), pointing the dependency outward against the layering the repository documents.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The ShipmentRepository port declares well over fifteen required operations; every consumer uses two or three of them and every implementation (and test double) has to provide all.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Shipment is an aggregate with state and no behaviour: every status change, label assignment and void is done by the application services writing its fields, so its invariants (a voided shipment has no active label) are enforced nowhere.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Shipment exposes its status, label and parcels as public writable fields (and the parcels array itself), so any caller can put it into an invalid state.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The test exercises label creation and asserts nothing: it passes whatever the service returns.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A skipped test with no reason, issue or condition recorded: nobody can tell whether it is obsolete or hiding a bug.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The act and the assertion run inside a try whose catch discards everything, including the assertion error: the test cannot fail.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Every collaborator of the route (calculator, registry, cache, logger, clock) is replaced by a mock and the test asserts the mocks were called: it tests the wiring it set up, not the behaviour.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A flat (carrier, service level) to product-code switch: many case labels, no nesting, one-line arms. A lookup table, not complex logic.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The same flat switch: nothing nests, nothing interacts; a reader takes in one arm at a time.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated from the rate-card CSV by tools/generate-zones.mjs, with a header saying so; never edited by hand. Its size is data, not authored code.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated lookup switch (see TRP-003); not authored logic.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated lookup function (see TRP-003); its length is the size of the table.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The API's address contract and the Alder adapter's wire address are an intentional pair of small data shapes in different boundaries: they change for different reasons (our API versioning vs the carrier's schema). Data only, no logic.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The other half of the DTO pair (TRP-006).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The catch logs the failure with the label id and path and then rethrows: the log adds context the caller does not have. Not a pointless rethrow, not a swallowed error.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The same catch: it logs and rethrows, nothing is swallowed.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: 'TODO' here is a carrier status code in a string literal (Corvid's 'to do' state for a parcel not yet collected), not a comment marking unfinished work.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A documented URL path segment of the carrier's tracking API inside a string literal, not a debt marker.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: One line, one named rule, with the reason after the double dash: the regular expression strips control characters from field data on purpose, which is exactly what no-control-regex warns about.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: @ts-expect-error with a reason in a test that deliberately passes an ill-typed value to prove the runtime guard rejects it; unlike @ts-ignore it fails the build if the error ever disappears.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Deliberate fire-and-forget with the reason in a comment: refresh() catches and logs every failure itself, so the voided promise can never reject.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Many small methods that all read the same rate table and thresholds: cohesive, however many methods it has.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: quote.ts and surcharge-policy.ts refer to each other's types only, with import type: the imports are erased at compile time, so there is no runtime cycle.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A hooks interface whose members are all optional callbacks: an implementer provides only the hooks it needs, so the member count burdens nobody.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A data-shape interface (a response contract) with many fields and no operations: there is nothing to segregate.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: LabelBatch exposes its labels through a getter that returns a read-only copy, and its id as a readonly field; all changes go through its methods.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A run-to-completion CLI reads its manifest synchronously inside its async main: there is no event loop serving anyone else, so blocking costs nothing.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The template interpolates a module constant only: the message is the same text on every call, so nothing that belongs in a field is baked into it.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The expensive debug serialisation runs only inside an isLevelEnabled('debug') guard.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A regular expression that validates the shape of a tracking number, an identifier, not a structured format.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Both stdout and stderr of lpstat are read to the end.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The truncation loop's condition has a floor (text.length > 0): it stops at the empty string.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: importArchive changes the working directory and restores it in a finally block, on every path.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Upper-case labels under switch (code.toUpperCase()): every arm is reachable.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An unparsable cut-off time falls back to the documented default and logs a warning that names the bad value: neither silent nor invented.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Used by the rate-card CLI under tools/ (and its tests), not by the service: an export with a consumer outside src is not dead.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: RateCalculator is handed the rate-card source (the disposable cache in production) by the composition root and does not dispose it: it does not own it; the composition root disposes it on shutdown.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `log` here is the import command's console sink (ImportLog writes a line for the operator to stdout), not a structured logger: a formatted human message is what it is for.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An interface of optional method signatures: there is no control flow in the file at all. The `?` of an optional member is not a branch.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A three-command CLI dispatcher (a switch with one usage check per command, cyclomatic 11): flat, short and read one arm at a time; well under any reasonable function-complexity budget.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: parseAddress is flat field validation (one single-line check per required field plus a table-driven postcode check), cyclomatic 12: each condition stands alone and reads at a glance; below any reasonable function budget.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A conditional skip whose condition is the reason (no lp binary on the machine) and whose comment says so.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The test asserts through a local helper (expectProblem) that calls expect: it has assertions, just not inline.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One genuinely over-complex method (CH-001) among roughly two hundred small functions: a real but bounded deduction. The generated lookup and the flat switch add nothing.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Same reasoning as BND-001 for the nested decision tree of CH-002.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One copy-pasted pair of carrier-adapter members (CH-006) in a ~3 kLoC codebase: a small density of clones.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One low-cohesion class (CH-007) among a few dozen cohesive ones.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Every source file is TypeScript under strict compiler options; only the tools build relaxes strict null checks.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Unit and HTTP-level tests import nearly every production module; a few infrastructure modules (the printer, the CLI entry) are reached only partly.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: package.json wires test, lint, typecheck and format scripts.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Mostly idiomatic TypeScript naming, but the messy legacy parts mix styles (snake_case locals, Hungarian-style prefixes, abbreviations). Judged by a model on a sample: wide band.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: The clean parts carry few, purposeful comments; the messy parts have comments that restate the code and one that is stale. Judged by a model on a sample: wide band.
